subject: Storage mesh eviction semantics & partner SLAs
messages:
From: Maria Lopez <maria@pinecone.io>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 08:15:00 -0700
Subject: Questions re: eviction behavior for hybrid storage mesh

Hi Neha / team,

Thanks again for the demo last week — we were excited to see the S3 cold-tier integration in action. As we start scoping a joint integration, a few technical questions popped up from our engineers around eviction semantics and what Redwood expects from a vector store when a document moves to cold storage:

- Can Redwood surface per-vector pin/priority metadata to upstream vector stores so partners can respect "do-not-evict" hints?
- What is your acceptable rehydration window? In your demo you showed a <5s prefix rehydration; is that a hard requirement or configurable per-customer?
- How should we model index pinning (per-document vs per-collection) for cost attribution and eviction SLAs?

We're trying to map these answers into the SLOs we propose to customers. If helpful, we can sketch an SLA table (p95/p99 latency for cache hit vs rehydrate, max staleness for cold reads). Would you be open to a quick workshop this week to align on a shared SLO matrix and a small set of integration knobs (pin TTL, priority, sync window)?

I can loop in Tom (Weaviate) and StorageOne if we want cross-vendor alignment.

Thanks,
Maria
Senior Solutions Engineer, Pinecone

Attachment: (none)
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Lopez <maria@pinecone.io>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 4 Jul 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions re: eviction behavior for hybrid storage mesh

Maria — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Short answers up front:

- Pin/priority metadata: yes — Redwood can propagate per-vector metadata (up to NKB) as routing hints. We treat these as "soft pins" unless there is an explicit tenant-level "pin forever" flag which we reserve for enterprise contracts.
- Rehydration window: default internal SLO is 5s p95 for first-token on rehydrated items when routing through our hot-cache. We can make that configurable per-deployment; for Dedicated customers we sometimes commit to sub-3s p95 with warm prefetching.
- Pinning model: recommend per-document pinning for fine-grained cost attribution; allow collection-level pins as a convenience but charge a higher reserve.

I've attached a short diff doc that outlines the behavioral hooks our runtime exposes (eviction-semantics-diff.md) and a first-pass SLA draft (sla-draft-v1.pdf). Can we do a 45m workshop Tuesday 7/6 10:00-10:45 PT? If that time doesn't work, propose two alternatives.

Next steps / asks for your team before the workshop:
- If Pinecone / Weaviate can confirm support for metadata pinning and a per-id pin API surface, add a short note in the shared doc.
- If partners have a preferred SLO table format, drop it into the Drive link.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Partnerships — Vector & Storage Ecosystem
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eviction-semantics-diff.md (text), sla-draft-v1.pdf (pdf)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 5 Jul 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Questions re: eviction behavior for hybrid storage mesh

Neha — quick internal notes (cc'ing Vanessa + Karthik):

On our side I'd like us to be explicit about 3 negotiation levers for partners/customers:

1) Pin semantics taxonomy: "soft-pin" (best-effort, evict on extreme memory pressure) vs "hard-pin" (explicit reserved capacity, additional charge). We should include exact behavior under pressure (e.g., soft-pins may be evicted if host memory > 85%).
2) Rehydration SLO tiers: Standard (5s p95), Fast (3s p95 + prefetch buffer), Enterprise (1-2s p95 with dedicated warm pool). Map each tier to an estimated cost delta per 1M queries.
3) Staleness / consistency model when rehydrating from S3: eventual with TTL windows vs synchronous read-through for cold reads (customer choice).

Also — legal will push back on any "forever pin" without an explicit commercial commitment. Add a line in the SLA doc making "forever" only available via dedicated reserve.

I'll draft the cost delta estimates after the workshop. Vanessa — do we want to own the doc with Pinecone or have them own the first draft of the SLO table?

-ben

Subject: Re: Questions re: eviction behavior for hybrid storage mesh

Thanks — this is super helpful. We can support per-id metadata pins and a pin/unpin API; we'll add language about "soft" vs "hard" pin behavior in our draft. We also have a recommended SLO table template which we've put in the shared Drive link (see below).

We've added a short note on index pinning semantics (per-id preferred) and a proposal for a "warm prefetch" flag that partners can set when customers subscribe to the Fast/Enterprise tiers.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/open?id=eviction-slas-workshop-2027 (we added 'pinecone-slo-template.csv')

Happy to run the Tuesday 7/6 slot. If you want Tom (Weaviate) looped in for cross-vendor alignment we can invite him — CC'ing StorageOne as an FYI.

Best,
Maria
